assumptions: The opportunity is judged at the planning and pre-validation stage; the absence of customers, paid pilots, and signed laboratory agreements is treated as uncertainty rather than proof of failure.
The network would act only as a procurement and logistics intermediary: the performing laboratory would retain technical control, sign the report, and own any accreditation claim.

The founder remains within the stated part-time limit while employed and uses AI, contractors, and laboratory specialists for automatable, legal, and method-specific work, without assuming that AI substitutes for accreditation expertise or partner relationships.
Laboratory access, reservations, and pricing would have to be negotiated on lawful commercial and non-discriminatory terms; no exclusive or discounted public-infrastructure access is assumed.
The stated pricing, margins, acquisition payback, project volume, startup capital, and founder-net-worth timeline are hypotheses rather than established economics.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Combining method-scope matching, sample custody, procurement, and turnaround management around mandatory or urgent testing is a coherent coordination insight. Its distinctiveness is only moderate because direct laboratories already provide substantial scoping and ordering support, while established platforms already orchestrate scientific procurement.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Regulatory, buyer, certification, and failure triggers can make testing necessary, and incumbent volume demonstrates paid demand for laboratory work. The packet does not isolate an SME segment with recurring procurement failure or show willingness to pay a 12-20% intermediary spread or priority membership when direct providers already quote and support customers.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: The model is asset-light and could generate repeat revenue without owning instruments. However, the spread, 45-62% gross margin, payback, 500-project volume, reservation costs, logistics losses, retests, liability allocation, and owner-earnings path are unsupported; the margin basis is also not reconciled with laboratory invoice pass-through, leaving the path to PLN 5 million of founder net worth speculative.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A substantial paid testing market plainly exists, but the proposed beachhead spans hardware, materials, cosmetics, food, biotech, and industrial SMEs. No narrow test family is ranked by urgency, order frequency, procurement failure, basket size, or incumbent service gap, so the first winnable and economically meaningful segment is not yet defined.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The candidate has not secured its intended control point: reserved slots, reseller authority, name use, or differentiated turnaround terms. Large integrated laboratories already combine technical sales, quotations, sampling, transport, and accredited methods, while mature procurement platforms establish that orchestration itself is not a unique position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful narrow wedge could extend into adjacent tests, compliance calendars, supplier quality workflows, more laboratories, and other Central European markets using shared intake, custody, and performance data. The upside is credible in shape, although each new method and industry adds technical, contractual, and operational complexity.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Turnaround history, method mappings, repeat-demand forecasts, and embedded compliance workflows could compound after meaningful volume. At present none is proprietary or proven, essential capacity rights are unsigned, public-infrastructure rules may limit exclusivity, and laboratories or established platforms could reproduce the service layer.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A reliable fixed-scope package with correct accreditation matching, custody, comparable reports, and reserved turnaround could materially reduce buyer effort and delay. The packet does not quantify a turnaround, price, accuracy, or convenience advantage over direct laboratories, several of which already provide close substitutes for much of the proposed journey.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Commercial access to Polish research infrastructure and the existence of procurement platforms show that the model is feasible in principle. No specific new regulatory, technological, cost, or buyer-behavior shift is evidenced that makes this intermediary unusually advantaged now, and the mature direct-service pattern may instead raise the entry bar.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Searchable fixed-scope menus and compliance-adviser referrals are plausible, testable channels compatible with the founder's preference for systematized selling. There is no observed adviser commitment, search CAC, conversion, repeat rate, or 1-3-order payback, and the network would compete with strong laboratory brands and direct technical-sales channels.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The asset-light concept can be piloted without laboratory capex and suits the founder's analytical and automation skills. Reliable delivery still requires method-specific judgment, continuously current accreditation mapping, reseller and name-use rights, custody and liability controls, partner management, and exception handling across industries; broad coverage is unlikely to fit the proposed part-time load before substantial narrowing and delegation.

main_structural_strength: An asset-light, trigger-driven managed-procurement layer can combine method matching, sample custody, logistics, and turnaround accountability while partner laboratories retain technical and accreditation responsibility; recurring compliance work could then produce useful demand and performance data.
primary_score_limiter: The proposal has not identified a narrow segment where buyers experience enough unresolved procurement or turnaround pain to pay an intermediary while laboratories grant usable reservation and resale terms at economics that survive direct-provider competition.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PORT, Hamilton, and TUV Rheinland already offer direct ordering, technical scoping, quotations, sampling or transport, and reports, while Science Exchange and Scientist.com already provide mature procurement orchestration; this materially challenges the claim that the proposed layer is sufficiently better or structurally scarce.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: For one narrowly defined test family, obtain a laboratory term sheet covering authorized resale, name use, current method scope, SLA or reservable capacity, cancellation, liability, and net pricing; then show paid SME pilots with invoice-level contribution margin, measurable turnaround improvement, quote-to-order conversion, acquisition cost, repeat behavior, and willingness to pay the spread.
highest_value_structural_change: Replace the broad cross-industry capacity network with a single-vertical managed compliance-testing subscription for one recurrent, time-sensitive test family: pre-map a small lab panel, sell an annual testing calendar and custody workflow, route each job transparently to the performing lab, and reserve capacity only after paid demand proves the required volume. This concentrates expertise and distribution, reduces speculative reservation exposure, and creates recurring workflow and data advantages.
